chunk_findings.detail: The added queue design makes each queued waiter hold an flock on its ticket file while waiting and poll every `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` seconds. This violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], which states agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. With multiple CI runs queued for the full-suite lock, every queued agent polls at 4 Hz while holding a lock, which is exactly the pattern the guidance forbids.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:QUEUE_POLL_S

chunk_findings.detail: The new code constructs `SuiteBusy(_holders(directory, limit), time.monotonic() - start, position)` both in the `say(...)` call and in the `raise`. The previous implementation called `SuiteBusy(holders, elapsed)` with only two arguments, and this diff does not update the `SuiteBusy` class. With any non-first waiter, the first time `position != said` it tries to build the exception and gets a `TypeError` instead of a `SuiteBusy` refusal, so the queue wait can crash before timing out or notifying.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: In `_live`, a `.ticket` is unlinked whenever `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` can acquire the lock; `age` is checked only on `LockTimeout`. A new or reclaimed `.ticket` is briefly an unlocked file between the rename/open in `_Ticket.__init__`/`__enter__` and the owner actually acquiring the flock. If another waiter scans in that window, it locks and deletes the ticket. The just-created waiter then has no visible directory entry, `_beat` fails on the missing path, and later `_live` scans never include it, so it is treated as last and can be passed by later arrivals.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_live

chunk_findings.detail: When a waiter times out, `_Ticket.__exit__` renames `self.path` to `.parked` without first calling `_beat`. The parked file keeps the last heartbeat `st_mtime`, not the parking time. If the final `_live()` scan before timeout takes longer than `grace_s`, the just-created parked file is already older than `grace_s`, so the next scanner treats it as expired and deletes it, losing the kept queue place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_Ticket.__exit__

chunk_findings.detail: The wait `_until(lambda: _tickets(tmp_path) == 1)` is not a valid barrier here. The first `early` attempt at line 138 has already created a `.ticket` file; for the later retry to keep its place, that ticket must still exist as `*.ticket` after `SuiteBusy`. Therefore `_tickets(tmp_path)` is already `1` before `late = _waiter(...)` is started, so this wait can return immediately before `late` has actually enqueued. The following `_until(lambda: _tickets(tmp_path) == 2)` can then be satisfied by the retained `early` ticket plus `late`'s new ticket before the `early` retry thread is scheduled; the outer holder is released with only `late` ready, making `order == ["early", "late"]` flaky or failing. The condition after starting `late` should require a count that cannot be satisfied by the retained early ticket (or otherwise wait for `late` to have its own ticket), otherwise the test does not exercise the intended “retry keeps place” interleaving deterministically.
